title: Hans Zimmer - Cornfield Chase (Interstellar OST, deluxe edition track 2): source map

source.decode_command: ffmpeg -i cornfield_chase.mp3 -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_f32le dec48.wav  (time 0 = first decoded sample; every time in this map uses this timeline)
source.license: user statement 2026-11-19: licensed for this video (see A/music/LICENSES.md)

beat_offset_note: beat k is at -0.033 + 0.625*k s (k = 0..191). Beat 0 = bar 1 downbeat sits 33 ms before the first sample (the file opens on the downbeat). Grid accuracy about +-10 ms; tempo is constant 96.000 BPM for the whole piece (no measurable drift over 88 s, < 5 ms). One beat = 30000 samples at 48 kHz, one bar = 90000, one cycle = 720000, so every loop or cut below is sample-exact on the click.
meter_note: Triple meter: chords change every 6 beats (2 bars of 3/4) and onset accents repeat every 3 beats (z = +2.3 to +3.2 vs 2- and 4-beat folds at z <= 0). Bar 18 (31.842 s) has only 2 beats: bar lines before it fall on beats = 0 mod 3, after it on beats = 2 mod 3. Bars are numbered 1..64 for music, bar line 65 = the hard stop at 119.342 s.

key.tonal_centre: A minor (A Aeolian; same notes as C major)
key.pedal: E (E4/E5 pedal with D# and F neighbour notes on top of every chord)
key.progression: F - G - Am - G, 2 bars (6 beats, 3.75 s) per chord, 8-bar cycle = 15.000 s (VI - VII - i - VII in A minor)
key.note: Key-profile correlation picks E minor only because the E pedal is constant; the bass (F, G, A) and the chords say A minor / C major. The cycle never cadences, which is why the piece feels suspended and forward-moving.

sections.name: intro_a
sections.description: Opening swell from near-silence (bars 1-2, RMS -60 to -45 dB), then the first chord cycle: sustained organ-like chords F (4 bars incl. swell) - G - Am - G under a constant high E pedal with D#/F neighbour notes (the soft "ticking" ostinato). Quiet, dark.

sections.name: intro_b
sections.description: Second chord cycle F - G - Am - G, same texture but gradually brighter: 3-8 kHz band rises about +6 dB at bar 11 and keeps climbing to bar 18 (upper-register layer joins, slow crescendo). Bar 18 is a 2-beat bar, so the last G lasts 5 beats.

sections.name: lift
sections.description: Bass drops out; a close, bright mid-register 16th-note figure around E4-E5 takes over (300 Hz-1 kHz +10 dB), ticking pulse clearly audible, no chord change (E pedal). Bar 23 (40.592 s) is the riser: low end and 3-8 kHz swell into the hit.

sections.name: arrival
sections.description: THE BURST at 42.467 s: massive low-register entry (+16 dB below 120 Hz, sample peak -0.2 dBFS, strongest transient of the piece), full organ texture, driving 16ths. Short chord cycle F - G - Am (no closing G).

sections.name: drive_1
sections.description: First full main cycle F - G - Am - G (15.000 s). High register grows: 3-8 kHz +5 dB, >8 kHz +7 dB by bar 34 (61.2 s).

sections.name: drive_2
sections.description: Second main cycle, brighter (spectral centroid 1.05 -> 1.3 kHz; >8 kHz +3 dB from bar 42, 76.2 s); low end still thin.

sections.name: build_1
sections.description: Deep low end returns at 83.717 s (+20 dB below 120 Hz): the second big lift, RMS steps up about 3.5 dB. Full, dense texture.

sections.name: build_2
sections.description: Steady crescendo, every band +1 to +4 dB across the cycle; the most loop-friendly material in the piece.

sections.name: peak
sections.description: Fullest and loudest bars (RMS about 3 dB above build_1, all bands at maximum). The music stops dead at 119.342 s, on a bar line in the middle of the G chord.

sections.name: tail
sections.description: Reverb tail after the hard stop: -6 dB at 119.35 s, -40 dB at 124.2 s, about -60 dB at 126 s; file ends 126.960 s.

percussion_note: No drum kit or percussion layer was found: the percussive/harmonic energy ratio stays between -12 and -19 dB in every bar. The rhythmic drive comes from the 16th-note ostinato (tatum 0.156 s); the only hit-like event is the harmonic low-register entry at 42.467 s.
instrument_note: Layer names are inferred from the spectrum (band energies, register, attack, harmonic/percussive split); they are not confirmed by ear.
climax_note: Fullest, loudest bars of the piece (bar 62 = F downbeat of the last cycle). Place the "aha" line on 113.717 (or on the equivalent bar after loops).
burst_note: Biggest single impact (low-register entry). Natural place for the first big reveal; 9.375 s of lift (bars 19-23) leads into it.

options: E1 (original): play through the peak, the music stops dead on the bar line 119.342 s, keep the reverb tail (fade the last 1 s after about 125.9 s). Dramatic stop, good for a final title card held in silence.

E2 (warm epilogue): after the peak, join to intro F (bar 11, 18.717 s, or bar 3, 3.717 s) at an F downbeat with a 0.625 s equal-power crossfade and let the quiet cycle fade out. Harmony continues (G -> F), the level drops about 20 dB on purpose (a breath, not a hidden seam).
E3: stop + tail as in E1, then bring back the opening swell (0 - 7.5 s, bars 1-4) under or after the tail and fade it out: the film ends where it began.

edit_rules: Cut, loop and join only at bar lines (beat k = -0.033 + 0.625 k; bar lines listed in bars[]). Every loop length below is a whole number of bars, so the beat and bar grid after a loop continues exactly (the edited track keeps 96 BPM and the same grid).

For a seamless loop the chord context must match on both sides (same chord and same bar-of-chord before and after the bar line): main body loops of 8 bars (15.000 s) or 4 bars (7.5 s) inside the same G-G pair.

Use the crossfade stored with each candidate (length, placement, law). "pre" = the fade ends 10 ms before the bar line, so the new downbeat attack comes cleanly from the in-side; equal-gain only where the two signals are strongly correlated (phase_rho > 0.5).
Do not loop back from build_1/build_2/peak into drive or intro: the deep bass that enters at 83.717 s would vanish (level jump 2-4 dB).
Tool: A/music/cc/py/cc_edit.py plan.json out.wav out_map.json renders any bar-level plan and writes the edited timing map (beats, bars, sections, climax, junctions).

scoring.quality: 0-100 context similarity of the two sides of the jump: 25% log-mel spectrum 0.4 s around the bar line, 20% log-mel over one bar, 25% chroma (harmony), 15% level match, 15% waveform correlation at the splice (phase continuity)
scoring.seam_test: test render with crossfades of 40, 156, 312 and 625 ms, centre or pre placement, equal-power or equal-gain; best one kept. Pass = level dip and bump <= 1.5 dB vs both original sides, spectral-flux ratio <= 1.15, no new click above 6 kHz (<= +1 dB), spectral jump across the seam no more than 1.5 dB above the natural change at that bar line
scoring.rendered_seam: log-mel change across the seam in the rendered file (0.3 s and 1 bar each side), as a percentile of the same change at natural bar lines inside sections of the original. Below 75 means at least a quarter of the composer's own bar lines change the sound more than this seam; below 50 means the seam changes less than a typical bar line.
scoring.score: 0.5 x quality + 0.25 x (100 - pct short) + 0.25 x (100 - pct bar); x0.8 if the seam test fails. Grade A = score >= 65, seam pass and both percentiles <= 75; B = score >= 50 and seam pass; else C.
